inlines.v: THEY, pronoun plural ; objective case, them.] 1. The men, the women, the animals, the things. It is never used adjectively, but always as a pronoun referring to persons, or as a substitute referring to things. THEY and their fathers have transgressed against me. Ezekiel 2:3. THEY of Italy salute you. Hebrews 13:10. Blessed are they who hunger and thirst after righteousness. Matthew 5:4. 2. It is used indefinitely, as our ancestors used man, and as the French use on. they say, [on dit, ] that is, it is said by persons, indefinitely.
